reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) describes the corrosion resistance of HEA coatings on Q235 steel, not the corrosion mechanism of untreated Q235 steel itself. Neither passage provides data on defect-driven initiation, non-protective oxide formation, or temperature effects on anodic dissolution in the base metal, leaving all key premises unsupported by the cited prior work.
premises: Localized corrosion in Q235 steel initiates at microstructural defect sites (grain boundaries, inclusions, surface heterogeneities).
Non-protective oxide films form at these defect sites.
Elevated temperature increases anodic dissolution kinetics at defect sites.
Reducing surface defect density improves corrosion resistance (lower icorr, less pitting, more noble OCP).
